newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain not planning budget adjustment - Folgado.
newsitem.headline: Spain not planning budget adjustment - Folgado.

text.p: Spain is not preparing any additional adjustment to public expenditure given the shortfall in Social Security income, Budget Secretary Jose Folgado said on Monday.
"The state is not undertaking any special adjustment to compensate for problems at the Social Security," Folgado told journalists.
Economists estimate the shortfall at between 150 and 200 billion pesetas, given lower-than-expected revenues.

Folgado also said he sees the Spanish central government deficit narrowing, and falling under the 1996 goal of 3.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP). The objective for the overall deficit is 4.4 percent of GDP this year.
"It is very likely that the central government deficit will be below 3.5 percent at the end of the year," Folgado said.
In October, the central government deficit was 2.4 percent of GDP.

According to Folgado, budget data so far this year suggests that the central administration deficit will fulfill the government's target, while the regional administrations' finances are also likely to come in on target.
"We can guarantee we will fulfill the budget deficit," Folgado said.
